title: Milne’s rationality conjecture and algebraic specialization
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Hodge classes on abelian varieties, after reduction mod p, pair to the same rational number in every cohomology theory and are cut out by one algebraic cycle.
constructive: no - existence of cycles via CM Hodge theorem
opportunity: None. Pure arithmetic geometry (motives/standard conjectures); no computation anyone performs depends on it.
caveats: Depends on 032 (rational Hodge for CM abelian varieties), same research cluster as the Oct-7 withdrawn Weil-class/K3 papers though 032 itself is not withdrawn; unformalized.

title: The full BSD formula from low Selmer corank
subject: Number theory
plain_english: For every elliptic curve over Q of (analytic) rank 0 or 1, the exact Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer formula holds at every prime, so the 'analytic order of Sha' that databases compute is the true order of the Tate-Shafarevich group.
constructive: partial - theorem is an identity; per-curve verification only needs rigorous rank<=1 certification, which LMFDB/Sage already do
opportunity: Rank 0 and 1 curves are the bulk of the Cremona/LMFDB tables. Today Sha for them is listed as 'analytic' and Sage's prove_BSD() returns a list of primes p for which BSD(E,p) could not be proven (it chains 2-descent, Kolyvagin, Kato, Lawson-Wuthrich, etc.). If 002 holds, every analytic-rank<=1 curve gets the full formula, so LMFDB could flag the Sha column as proven and prove_BSD could return [] once analytic rank<=1 is rigorously certified. Arithmetic-statistics users who now caveat 'assuming BSD' benefit.
first_step: Open an LMFDB/Sage discussion ticket (not a merge): propose a 'BSD formula proven for analytic rank <=1 (OpenAI preprint, unrefereed)' flag and a prove_BSD short-circuit gated on rigorous r_an<=1; hold until independent expert review of the three manuscripts.
caveats: Extraordinary claim (full BSD in rank<=1 was open); 3 interlocking unformalized manuscripts plus companion Goldfeld/Smith inputs; Oct-7 revision removed a citation to a removed supporting manuscript. Rank-1 curves need a rigorous L'(E,1)!=0 certificate.

title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
subject: Number theory
plain_english: No Dirichlet L-function (including zeta) has a zero with real part > 7/8, and there are no Landau-Siegel zeros. Consequently the least quadratic non-residue mod p is at most C(log p)^A, so square roots mod p (deterministic Tonelli-Shanks) and Miller's primality test run in deterministic polynomial time without GRH.
constructive: yes for corollaries - scan 2,3,... with Legendre symbol, then Tonelli-Shanks; the stopping rule needs no constant
explicit_constants: Half-plane 7/8 has no constants. n(p) <= C(log p)^A with A=32 via Bhargava-Ivanyos-Mittal-Saxena (direct explicit formula gives about 2/(1-7/8)=16); C is effective but never computed. Landau-Siegel constant c is not explicit (proof by contradiction). Cor. PNT in APs with error x^{11/12} log x, effective but not explicit.
opportunity: This is a certification result, not a software one. Textbook and complexity statements become unconditional: 'square roots mod p, deterministic poly time (was GRH)', Vinogradov's n(p)<<p^eps, effective h(D)>>sqrt|D|/loglog|D|, and effective PNT in progressions; Galbraith §2.9, Cohen, Crandall-Pomerance, Shoup and Wikipedia can drop the GRH caveat. In practice nothing changes. (log p)^16..32 is about 10^46..10^91 at 1024 bits. It beats the unconditional Burgess bound p^0.152 only above roughly 1000 bits (about 2200 bits for the paper's A=32), and that is before the uncomputed constant C, while OpenSSL BN_mod_sqrt tries at most ~80 candidates and FLINT n_quadratic_nonresidue scans. AKS/Lenstra-Pomerance is already better than a deterministic Miller test. KEY NEGATIVE: the GRH dependence in PARI bnfinit/quadclassunit/bnfisnorm, Magma ClassGroup Proof:="GRH", Sage proof=False and CSI-FiSh's CSIDH-512 class group concerns Hecke L-functions of class-group characters of K, not Dirichlet L-functions. 003 does not cover them (only K=Q(sqrt-3)), so those caveats must stay.
targets: Galbraith 'Mathematics of Public Key Cryptography' §2.9 (Tonelli-Shanks remark)
Wikipedia: Tonelli-Shanks, Quadratic residue, Miller-Rabin (deterministic variants)
first_step: Write a 2-page note: derive an explicit unconditional n(p) <= C(log p)^16 from Re(rho) <= 7/8 plus explicit zero-counting, compute the crossover against explicit Burgess-type bounds (Trevino), and state plainly that PARI/Magma/Sage class-group GRH caveats are unaffected. Send it to FLINT/PARI maintainers as docs-only.
caveats: Top-line 7/8 theorem and the Landau-Siegel gap are Lean-formalized (comparator configs with standard axioms only; no sorry/axiom in OAI tree by grep; I did not rebuild). The corollaries are classical implications and are not formalized. The 11/12 alternate proof is independent. All algorithmic consequences are galactic.
evidence: /root/openai-math/preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-October-5-2026/build/paper2.tex thm:main, cor:primes-ap, intro consequences (Miller test, h(D), idoneal numbers)
PARI General_number_fields GRH notes; Magma ClassGroup handbook; CSI-FiSh eprint 2019/498; OpenSSL bn_sqrt.c (web)

title: Hilbert’s tenth problem over ℚ
subject: Number theory
plain_english: No algorithm can decide whether an integer polynomial (any number of variables) has a rational root, even restricted to degree <= 4, or to sums of squares of quadrics.
constructive: no - impossibility theorem (reduction is effective; H10(Q) has Turing degree 0')
opportunity: This is a 'stop searching for a complete algorithm' result for problems equivalent to rational solvability. Rational realizability of matroids is equivalent to H10(Q) (Sturmfels 1987, quoted in the OSCAR matroid paper), so it is now undecidable. Exact tensor rank over Q is polynomial-time equivalent to polynomial systems over Q by Shitov's integral-domain theorem (verify the reduction), so it is undecidable too. Requiring rational (not real-algebraic) models in nonlinear arithmetic is also undecidable. Real SMT (QF_NRA, decidable via CAD/nlsat) and integer NIA (already undecidable) are unaffected, so the SMT channel is thin.
targets: SMT-LIB/Z3/cvc5 docs on rational-model requests for NRA
first_step: Check the exact form of the Sturmfels and Shitov reductions (many-one, unbounded variables). If they compose, add a one-line remark to the OSCAR matroid realizability docs and a short note for the tensor-rank community.
caveats: Undecidability needs an unbounded number of variables; fixed-dimension problems (rational points on curves/surfaces) are untouched. Depends on companion 2-converse (2nd manuscript) and 2-adic Fontaine-Mazur (010); unformalized.

title: Irrationality of Catalan’s constant
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Catalan's constant G = 1 - 1/9 + 1/25 - ... is irrational.
opportunity: None. Irrationality of a constant has no computational consequence (no irrationality measure provided).

title: Goldfeld’s conjecture: densities and mean analytic rank
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Among quadratic twists of any elliptic curve over Q, half have analytic rank 0 and half rank 1, and the average rank tends to 1/2.
opportunity: None directly. Its role is as an input to 002 (density-one BSD) and 004. Arithmetic statistics only.
caveats: Uses Smith's Selmer distribution results; unformalized.

title: Ordinary two-point correlations and the corrected Elliott conjecture
subject: Number theory
plain_english: The Liouville function at n and at a shifted/scaled n are asymptotically uncorrelated (two-point Chowla), with a log-power saving.
opportunity: None. Pseudorandomness of multiplicative functions is not used in any PRNG or test suite.

title: The Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture
subject: Number theory
plain_english: The Grothendieck-Teichmuller Lie algebra is free on one generator in each odd weight >= 3; hence H^0 of Kontsevich's graph complex is known.
constructive: partial - integral generators are chosen; non-canonical
opportunity: None practical. The only remote channel is deformation quantization / multiple-zeta-value bookkeeping in Feynman-integral codes, which already rely on Brown's results and computed data through high weight.
caveats: Lean-formalized; does not imply the MZV dimension (period) conjecture.

title: Function-field reconstruction from Milnor K-theory and Galois data
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Function fields of dimension >= 2 over algebraically closed fields can be reconstructed from mod-l Milnor K-theory or abelian-by-central Galois data.
opportunity: None. Anabelian geometry with no computational counterpart.

title: Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Every odd irreducible 2-dimensional 2-adic Galois representation of Q (finitely ramified) appears in a completed Hecke algebra; de Rham ones with distinct weights are modular (Fontaine-Mazur at p=2).
opportunity: None directly. It is an input to 004 (H10 over Q). Modular-forms databases already assume modularity in these cases.

title: Prime-factor statistics of $`p-1`$
subject: Number theory
plain_english: For a random prime p, the sizes of the prime factors of p-1 follow the Poisson-Dirichlet (Dickman) law; also there are x^{1-o(1)} primes p near x with p-1 being x^delta-smooth.
constructive: no - asymptotic distribution, no error term
explicit_constants: none; o(1) and limits without rates (Siegel-Walfisz inputs ineffective)
opportunity: This certifies, asymptotically, the heuristic that p-1 for a random prime behaves like a random integer. That heuristic is behind success-probability estimates for two-stage Pollard p-1 (joint law of the top two factors = B1/B2 success) and the old 'are strong primes needed' (Rivest-Silverman) / FIPS 186 auxiliary-prime debate. No rates, so it cannot certify any number at 512-4096 bits. Generation and test code is unchanged.
targets: FIPS 186-5 / OpenSSL bn_rsa_fips186_4.c auxiliary-prime rationale (docs only)
first_step: Only worth pursuing if someone extracts an effective error term; otherwise cite as asymptotic justification.
caveats: Says nothing about safe primes (P+(p-1)=(p-1)/2); unformalized; a counting statement over primes up to x, not for factors of a given RSA modulus.

title: Independent largest prime factors of consecutive integers
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Whether n is smooth and whether n+1 is smooth are asymptotically independent events (joint Dickman law); P+(n) < P+(n+1) half the time.
explicit_constants: none; limit for fixed exponents a,b, no rate
opportunity: Twin-smooth searches for isogeny crypto (B-SIDH, SQIsign parameter hunts by CHM/XGCD-and-boost/lattice SVP methods) budget yields with rho(u)^2 independence heuristics. 012 proves that independence asymptotically for fixed exponents, but gives no error term at n ~ 2^256, so it certifies nothing numerically. SQIsign variants now use p = c*2^e - 1, which shrinks the need.
targets: twin-smooth search literature (B-SIDH, SQIsign parameter generation; arXiv 2509.17699)

title: Ostmann’s inverse Goldbach conjecture

opportunity: None.

title: Restricted geometric Langlands, global Arthur enhancements, and generic Ramanujan
subject: Number theory

opportunity: None. (Ramanujan bounds over function fields can matter for explicit expander/Ramanujan-complex constructions, but those use GL_n/PGL_d cases already known; exceptional-group generic cases add no usable construction.)

opportunity: None. The tempting channel ('ideal lattices behave like random lattices', used in ideal-SVP/Ring-LWE heuristics) does not apply: crypto uses CM power-of-two cyclotomics, not primitive totally real fields, and no rate is given.

title: The irrationality exponent of π is 2
subject: Number theory
plain_english: pi cannot be approximated by fractions p/q much better than 1/q^2: |pi - p/q| >= q^{-2-eps} for all large q; the Flint-Hills series converges.
opportunity: None. The one channel, worst-case trigonometric argument reduction in libm/MPFR/CORE-MATH, needs an effective bound. Libraries use exhaustively computed worst cases or the effective measure mu(pi) <= 7.1, and an ineffective exponent 2 cannot replace either.
caveats: Lean-formalized; the paper states the threshold is not effective.

opportunity: None.

opportunity: None.

title: Squarefree quartics and power-free polynomial values
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Irreducible integer quartics with no fixed square divisor take squarefree values with the predicted density; (d-2)-power-free values for all degrees d >= 4.
opportunity: None. (Squarefree polynomial values feed ring-of-integers computations, but practical NFS/nfinit code uses local p-maximal rounds, not densities.)

title: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal’s function
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Any interval of C*k^2/(loglog k)^2 consecutive integers contains a number coprime to any given integer with k prime factors (Jacobsthal's function is quadratic).
constructive: no - existence bound; C not explicit
explicit_constants: absolute C, not made explicit (the paper says so)
opportunity: None, checked. Jacobsthal's function bounds the longest run of candidates a small-prime sieve can reject in incremental prime search (OpenSSL probable_prime delta loop, GMP mpz_nextprime). Run time there is governed by prime gaps, and OpenSSL restarts with fresh randomness when delta exceeds ~2^64. Exact j(P_k) and h(k) are already computed for k <= 43-50 (Hajdu-Saradha, Ziller, Costello-Watts), so no code or guarantee changes.

title: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Inhomogeneous Duffin-Schaeffer: if sum phi(q)psi(q)/q diverges then almost every x has infinitely many q with ||qx - gamma|| < psi(q).
opportunity: None realistic. Real interference alignment in wireless DoF theory uses multidimensional Khintchine-Groshev for linear forms; this is 1-dimensional and almost-everywhere.

opportunity: None. It confirms the known non-uniformity of incremental prime search (primes after long gaps are favoured; Brandt-Damgard), which practice already accepts.

constructive: partial - finite periodic sieve obstruction exists, but bound B_D is nonexplicit

title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Every integer base that is not -1 or a square is a primitive root mod infinitely many primes (Artin's conjecture, infinitude part), with at least c_a x/log^2 x such primes in (x,2x). The analytic engine is a uniform zero-free strip Re s > 1-10^-6 for all finite-order Hecke L-functions of cyclotomic fields containing mu_12.
constructive: no - counting lower bound; primes are found by search in practice
explicit_constants: c_a, x_a depend on base, not explicit; strip width 10^-6 is explicit
opportunity: (1) Coding theory: asymptotic existence results for quasi-cyclic, double-circulant and quasi-twisted codes stated 'assuming Artin's conjecture' (need infinitely many primes with 2 or q primitive) become unconditional where only infinitude is needed. This is the same structural condition BIKE (r prime, 2 primitive mod r) and HQC use for irreducible (X^r-1)/(X-1), though their concrete parameters never needed the conjecture. Results needing positive density remain conditional, because x/log^2 x is density zero. (2) Non-obvious: the Hecke strip transfers by Artin factorization to every Hecke L-function of every abelian number field, including class-group characters of quadratic fields. That yields unconditional, effective Bach-type generator bounds of order (log|d|)^{O(10^6)}. This is galactic: PARI bnfinit/quadclassunit, Magma's GRH bound and CSI-FiSh class-group certification stay GRH-conditional in practice. Same story as 142's factorization exponent 10^12.
targets: coding-theory literature conditioned on Artin (e.g. arXiv:1703.03109 quasi-polycyclic codes; double-circulant GV results)
BIKE/HQC design rationale docs (no parameter change)
first_step: Compile the list of coding/sequence-design theorems stated 'under Artin's conjecture' and sort them into 'needs infinitude only' (now unconditional) vs 'needs positive density' (still open). Separately, write out the Artin-factorization argument that the 10^-6 strip covers all abelian Hecke L-functions, and quantify the resulting Bach-type exponent to document that it is galactic.
caveats: Unformalized; the uniform cyclotomic Hecke strip is an extraordinary claim that also underpins 142; companion simultaneous-roots paper is conditional on four stated inputs; uses 011's PD-law marked Type II estimate as input.

title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
subject: Number theory
plain_english: Every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field is modular (matches a Bianchi automorphic form).
opportunity: LMFDB's elliptic-curves-over-number-fields section says modularity 'has not yet been proved for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields in general' and its completeness is 'assuming modularity'. 030 would make the IQ tables provably complete within their Bianchi level bounds. It would also justify L-function computations for these curves (analytic continuation/functional equation used by Dokchitser-style lfun code, BSD checks) without a modularity caveat. Previously only cases like X_0(15)(K) rank 0 (Caraiani-Newton) were covered.
targets: PARI lfun / Magma LSeries for curves over IQ fields (docs)
first_step: File an LMFDB issue proposing a qualified completeness statement ('modularity proven in OpenAI preprint 030, unrefereed') for IQ fields; do not drop caveats until refereed.
caveats: Single unformalized manuscript relying on Caraiani-Newton lifting; database completeness also depends on the Bianchi-form computations themselves.

title: Single-fold Diophantine representations and undecidability under an at-most-one-solution promise
subject: Mathematical logic
plain_english: Every recursively enumerable set has a Diophantine representation with exactly one witness per member, so integer polynomial solvability stays undecidable even when promised at most one solution (fixed number of variables and degree).
constructive: no - existence of the polynomial; coefficients and constants not displayed (paper says so)
explicit_constants: m, D exist but not given
opportunity: Essentially none. The only conceivable consumer is QF_NIA solvers exploiting uniqueness of solutions, and none do; integer nonlinear arithmetic was already undecidable. It is a clean citation for 'uniqueness promises do not help', no more.
caveats: Lean-formalized main theorem; the at-most-one-promise corollary is not separately formalized.

title: Separating choiceless counting from polynomial time and witnessed choice
subject: Mathematical logic
plain_english: Choiceless Polynomial Time with counting, long the leading candidate logic for PTIME on unordered structures, cannot express a simple polynomial-time query: consistency of a linear system over F_3. Adding witnessed symmetric choice strictly helps.
constructive: yes - explicit query and explicit separating structure pairs A_{b0}, A_{b1} built on 3-D box grids
opportunity: This redirects descriptive-complexity research away from CPT toward logics with linear algebra (solvability/rank logics FPS_3/FPR_3 do define the query). The non-obvious channel is ML expressivity. Permutation-invariant, choiceless architectures (GNNs, set/hypergraph networks whose power is bounded by CPT-like symmetric computation) provably cannot decide F_3-linear consistency without symmetry-breaking (random features, orderings). The paper's A_{b0}/A_{b1} pairs are concrete hard instances stronger than the CFI graphs used in GNN expressivity benchmarks such as BREC.
targets: descriptive complexity / graph canonization research (Grohe, Pakusa, Lichter)
first_step: Generate the paper's A_{b0}/A_{b1} structure pairs for small L as graphs and test whether current higher-order/subgraph GNNs separate them, as a BREC-style extension.
caveats: The theorem bounds CPT, not specific neural models. Linking it to a given architecture needs a simulation argument; most practitioners already break symmetry. Both results Lean-formalized.

title: Weak normalization implies strong normalization in pure type systems
subject: Mathematical logic
plain_english: In any pure type system, if every well-typed term has some normal form then every reduction sequence terminates (weak normalization implies strong normalization, beta only).
constructive: yes - reducibility-candidate construction; formalized in Lean
opportunity: A metatheory tool for proof-assistant foundations. For any PTS-shaped calculus, proving WN suffices for SN, so kernels may use any reduction strategy. Real kernels (Rocq/Coq CIC with inductives, fixpoints, cumulativity and eta; Lean 4 with proof irrelevance and quotients; Agda) are not PTSs. MetaCoq still assumes normalization axiomatically, and no WN-only proof is known for those systems. Transfer would need extending the profile-graph candidate technique to beta-eta and inductives, which is open research.
first_step: Ask MetaCoq/Lean4Lean metatheory authors whether a WN=>SN lemma for beta-eta plus inductives would let them replace an SN axiom with a WN proof; if not, close.
caveats: beta only (eta excluded); system-wide WN hypothesis still has to be proven; Lean-formalized.
